```{r}

library(p8105.datasets)
library(tidyverse)
data("ny_noaa")

ny_noaa

ny_noaa_df = ny_noaa |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  separate(date, into = c("year", "month", "day"), sep = "-") |>
  mutate(
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10, 
    year = as.numeric(year),
    month = as.numeric(month),
    day = as.numeric(day))
  
#used AI for finding out how to separate; specifically sep = "-"
  
ny_noaa_df

```

The original dataset is a tibble that is 7 columns and 2,595,176 rows. The data is divided by ID number which appears to be the same for each row. Other key variables are `date`, `pcrp`, 
`snow`, `snwd`, `tmax`, and `tmin`. 


```{r}

ny_noaa_df |> 
  count(snow, name = "n_obs") |>
  arrange(desc(n_obs)) |>
  filter(min_rank(desc(n_obs)) < 11) |>
  knitr::kable()
  
#Used arrange to order from most common to least
#Filter helps make the list smaller

```

Some of the most commonly observed values for snowfall include 0 mm, NA, 25 mm, 13 mm,and 51 mm. 0mm being first makes sense since it doesn't snow in New York at lot over the course of the year.

#Looking at average max temperature now

```{r}

ny_noaa_df |>
  filter(month %in% c(1,7)) |>
  mutate(month = case_when(
    month == 1 ~ "January",
    month == 7 ~ "July")) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y=mean_tmax, color = id)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .5) +
  facet_grid(. ~ month) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
  
#Used AI assistance to mutate using case_when to switch numbers to month terms. Also used AI assistance to get rid of the legend by using theme(legend.position = "none")

  
```

The mean temperature in January is much lower compared to the mean temperature in July. This result is expected. The temperature fluctuates more in January in a zig zap (up and down) appearance over the years. The temperature in July appears to have less variation. There are some outliers in the graphs. For instance, one outlier shows a very cold July year around 1988.


```{r}

tmax_tmin =
  ny_noaa_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_hex() +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Temperature (Max vs. Min)",
    x = "min (C)",
    y = "max (C)"
    )

#using geom_hex() here since lots of data

snow_dist =
  ny_noaa_df |> 
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = snow)) +
  geom_bin2d() +
  labs( 
    title = "Snowfall (0-100mm)",
    x = "year",
    y = "snowfall (mm)"
  )
  
#used geom_bin2d()

library(patchwork)

tmax_tmin + snow_dist
  


```
#Problem 2 on Accelerometers (wearable sensors)

```{r}

nhanes_covar_df = 
  read_csv(file = "./nhanes_covar.csv", skip = 4, na = c("NA", ".", "")) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  filter(age >= 21) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(
    sex = case_when(
      sex == 1 ~ "male",
      sex == 2 ~ "female"),
    sex = factor(sex), 
    education = case_when(
      education == 1 ~ "Less than high school",
      education == 2 ~ "High school equivalent",
      education == 3 ~ "More than high school"),
    education = forcats::fct_relevel(
      education, c("Less than high school", "High school equivalent", "More than high school")))
    
#using case_when again here, got from AI assistance unsure where it is in notes
#factor() to convert to categorical
#used AI assistance here to help identify which variables need to be reclassified and strategize how to approach

#using forcats:fct_relevel() since working with factors, and reordered it into those 3 groups

nhanes_covar_df
#has some extra info at top originally so need to skip that

nhanes_accel_df =
    read_csv(file = "./nhanes_accel.csv") |>
    janitor::clean_names() |>
    pivot_longer(
      starts_with("min"),
      names_to = "minute",
      names_prefix = "min",
      values_to = "mims") |>
    mutate(minute = as.numeric(minute))

#whenever really long data going across with same variable, you want to pivot longer

nhanes_accel_df

nhanes_df = left_join(nhanes_covar_df, nhanes_accel_df, by = "seqn")

nhanes_covar_df |>
  count(education, sex) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = n) |>
  knitr::kable()

```
In the less than high school category, there is 28 females and 27 males. In the high school equivalent category, there is 23 females and 35 males. In the more than high school category, there is 59 females and 56 males. 

```{r}
nhanes_covar_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = sex, y= age)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_grid(. ~ education)
  
#used facet_grid to clearly separate education
```
